preamble: Assibilation of the palatalized alveolar stop [tʲ] to the voiceless alveolo-palatal affricate [tɕ], with the palatal secondary articulation absorbed into a fricated release at the alveolo-palatal place. In Polish, dentals softened before front vowels were turned into the affricates ć, dź in the 12th century, so soft [tʲ] became ć/ci [tɕ]: Proto-Slavic *tixъ gave cichy (adverb cicho /ˈt͡ɕi.xɔ/), *tělo gave ciało /ˈt͡ɕa.wɔ/ and *teplъ gave ciepły /ˈt͡ɕɛ.pwɘ/, whereas East Slavic kept the stop (Russian тихий, тёплый). Kashubian went through the same stage and later depalatalized the affricate to c (cepłi, cało).

examples.from: Proto-Slavic *tixъ 'quiet' (soft t before *i; cf. Russian ти́хий)
Proto-Slavic *teplъ 'warm' (soft t before *e; cf. Russian тёплый)
